- Protective factors: Patient lives alone but is aware and responsive; communication with clinician; ambulance requested promptly
- Psychological impact: Acute stress reaction secondary to suspected cardiac event; no evidence of underlying psychiatric disorder disclosed in transcript

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Anxiety/stress reaction related to acute coronary syndrome suspicion
- Patient Goal(s): To remain calm and compliant with medical care; to reduce anxiety related to acute event
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide psychological support and reassurance during emergency care; monitor for any acute mental health symptoms
- Actions (Patient): Maintain communication with clinicians; disclose any worsening anxiety or distress
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide support and reassurance during ambulance transfer; advise emergency unit of allergy to aspirin and psychological state; monitor for risk symptoms

Secondary Problem: Not applicable

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of chest discomfort; importance of ambulance arrival; aspirin allergy; expected hospital assessment procedures including ECG
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Not recorded (acute medical emergency prioritized)
- Coping Strategies: Provided verbal reassurance; advised to stay calm; maintain open communication

- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: To be determined post-acute medical stabilization

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) / myocardial infarction  
  Likelihood: High  
  Justification: Classic angina symptoms (central chest pressure, radiation to left arm), associated nausea, diaphoresis, shortness of breath, multiple cardiovascular risk factors, ongoing symptoms at examination  
- Aortic dissection  
  Likelihood: Low to Medium  
  Justification: Chest discomfort radiating to left shoulder and arm, but pain described as pressure rather than tearing; absence of neurological or vascular signs  
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)  
  Likelihood: Low  
  Justification: Nausea and chest discomfort present but chest pain and systemic symptoms atypical; cardiac risk factors favor cardiac diagnosis  

Quality checks  
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Mental health follow-up plan post-acute care not documented; contact details missing  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None
